parts.name: Drum excavator
parts.basis: Counter-rotating bucket drums of NASA's ISRU Pilot Excavator, a 30 kg-class robot building on RASSOR 2 that digs 42 kg of regolith an hour; the drums need gravity to hold the regolith, so they work on the Moon and Mars. Mass taken as a third of the robot and power not published: both estimated.

parts.name: Drill with oven
parts.basis: Honeybee TRIDENT, the 1 m rotary-percussive drill of PRIME-1 and VIPER: 26.5 kg with its avionics, 50 W of rotary power (Zacny 2025); PVEx bakes out 80 percent of the water of the ice it cuts. Rates estimated; the oven's power is not published.

parts.name: Scoop
parts.basis: A scoop on an arm, lighter and cheaper than the drum excavator; it works in any gravity, microgravity included, on loose material and loose ice only. Rate, mass and power estimated.

parts.name: Wheeled chassis
parts.basis: The four-wheel skid-steer base of the ISRU Pilot Excavator, without suspension or steering actuators, for the Moon and Mars. Mass and power estimated.

parts.name: Anchored chassis
parts.basis: A frame that anchors itself to the surface of an asteroid or comet, where microgravity gives no traction. Mass and power estimated.

parts.name: Solar array
parts.basis: The ship's solar array, with its figures.

parts.name: Radioisotope generator
parts.basis: NASA's Multi-Mission Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator: about 110 W at the start of a mission from 4.8 kg of plutonium-238 dioxide, 45 kg. The materials besides the plutonium are estimated. Opened with Small modular fission, which opens plutonium-238.

parts.name: Battery and docking port
parts.basis: A 1 kWh battery at about 150 Wh a kilogram and the robot's side of a wireless charging dock, as Astrobotic's lunar wireless charger with WiBotic (125 W, under 3.3 kg for the whole system); it recharges at a charging station. Battery size estimated. Opened with Space batteries, which opens lithium-ion cells.

parts.name: Computer
parts.basis: An NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor class computer: 2,070 TFLOP/s of FP4 at up to 130 W. Mass with its carrier and housing estimated.
